subject: Order Form: Support SLO exceptions & maintenance blackout proposal
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@vectorscale.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@vectorscale.com; Miguel Torres <miguel@vectorscale.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Order form SLO asks and maintenance blackout request

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the draft order form. Procurement and the engineering leadership ran a quick read and have three asks that need to be reflected before we can move to legal:

1) Uptime: we need a 99.99% monthly uptime commitment for our production tenant (VectorScale-PROD).
2) Maintenance: any maintenance that could impact availability must be limited to 0200–0400 PT and capped at 2h/month. Planned maintenance outside that window must require 30 days notice and customer consent.
3) Service credits: credits should start at a single severe incident (>=30m downtime) at 5% invoice, scaling to 50% for >24h, with no cap for cumulative incidents in a 12-month window.

We know these are aggressive; if there's a standard commercial path (Dedicated or SLA premium) that gives us this guarantee, please flag it. Attached the vector suggested redlines to the order form (attachment: Vector_OrderForm_v2.pdf).

Can you confirm next steps? We are aiming to finalize before our month-end procurement cycle.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Procurement, VectorScale
[Attachment: Vector_OrderForm_v2.pdf (pdf)]

Subject: Re: Order form SLO asks and maintenance blackout request

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clear asks. Looping in Legal (Laura) and CS/ops (Marissa, Naomi) to evaluate technical and contractual fit. Quick notes from my side:
- 99.99% is typically available as a Dedicated tier or with a commercial premium for hosted customers; need to confirm pricing delta.
- Maintenance windows: ops historically run rolling upgrades and recommend wider UTC windows for safety, but we can explore a limited blackout window for production if we align on carveouts (e.g., emergency patches).
- Service credit caps: Redwood usually caps credits at a set max (e.g., monthly credit cap = 100% of monthly fees historically), but we can propose scaling.

Laura/Marissa/Naomi — can you review Elena's redlines and share an initial counterproposal by EOD tomorrow? Elena, we'll try to get back with specific language and a proposed DocuSign-ready order form.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@vectorscale.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form SLO asks and maintenance blackout request

Jordan / Elena —

I've reviewed the Vector redlines attached. Summary of legal position and proposed counterpoints:

1) Uptime: 99.99% is materially stricter than our standard hosted guarantee and implies much heavier operational commitments. Recommend offering: 99.95% for Redwood Hosted (standard), and 99.99% as an add-on priced commitment for Redwood Dedicated (explicitly called out in the order form).

2) Maintenance blackout: we can accept a customer-preferred maintenance window (market hours) for planned maintenance provided it is mutually agreed and scheduled at least 14 days in advance. For critical security fixes, we need an exception clause that allows immediate action with notification; propose required post-facto incident report within 48 hours.

3) Service credits: we can accept a graduated credit table but must cap cumulative credits to a percentage of annual fees (propose 6 months' worth of fees as an upper bound) to avoid open-ended liability. Request VectorScale to accept audit/forensics cooperation obligations as a precondition.

I'm attaching my redlines to the MSA (Redline_MSA_JB_comments.docx) with inline language. If Vector insists on uncapped credits or 99.99 for hosted without commercial uplift we will need C-suite approval.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redline_MSA_JB_comments.docx (docx)]

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@vectorscale.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form SLO asks and maintenance blackout request

Quick ops feasibility note from CS/Infra:

- 99.99% for multi-tenant hosted products has a high operational cost; to achieve that level for a production tenant we'd either need Dedicated hardware or a managed premium that includes hot standby capacity in the same region. We can outline both options in the order form and show the incremental cost.

- Maintenance windows: our safe operational pattern is to schedule rolling infra changes in a 00:00–06:00 UTC window to give engineers time to monitor post-deploy. Narrowing to 0200–0400 PT restricts our rollback options and increases blast radius.

Proposed compromise we can operate to (ops-friendly, customer-facing):
  * Redwood Hosted: 99.95% monthly uptime; maintenance will be scheduled within a mutually agreed 00:00–06:00 UTC window, with a maximum of 3 hours impacting a single tenant per month. Planned maintenance outside that window requires customer consent. Critical patches excluded with notification and post-incident report.
  * Redwood Dedicated / SLA Premium: 99.99% uptime option available as an add-on; Dedicated comes with a warm spare and prioritized scheduling for non-disruptive patching.
  * Service credits: tiered schedule starting at 5% for incidents >=30 minutes, 25% at >=6 hours, 50% at >=24 hours. Cumulative credits within a 12-month period capped at 6 months of fees; operational cooperation required for incident review.

I've attached the ops runbook excerpts that describe our maintenance approach and how we measure per-tenant impact. If Vector gets Dedicated, many of their asks become straightforward.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success & Reliability, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ops-runbook-maintenance.pdf (pdf)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form SLO asks and maintenance blackout request

Elena —

Thanks for the patience. Summarizing the proposed compromise so we can lock language into the order form and route to DocuSign:

1) Uptime: Redwood proposes 99.95% monthly uptime for Hosted (no change to price). 99.99% is available as a Dedicated/SLA Premium add-on; I will include a pricing appendix and the Dedicated order form option in the DocuSign packet.

2) Maintenance window: Planned maintenance will be scheduled within a mutually agreed 00:00–06:00 UTC window; maximum impact to the VectorScale production tenant of 3 hours per month. Planned maintenance outside that window will require explicit customer approval. Critical security patches are excluded; Redwood will provide notice and a post-incident report within 48 hours.

3) Service credits: tiered table as proposed by Marissa: 5% for >=30m, 25% for >=6h, 50% for >=24h. Cumulative credits within any 12-month period will be capped at the equivalent of 6 months of fees. Credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for availability failures and are conditional on customer cooperation with incident post-mortem and forensic requests.

Next steps: Laura will incorporate these points into the redlined MSA/order form; I will attach the Dedicated pricing appendix so Vector can choose that path if desired. Please confirm by EOD Monday 11/8 if this alignment works for VectorScale and I'll send the DocuSign packet.

Jordan Blake
